description: Runnable seed fixtures for intake and technical writing. The 36-scenario Excel workbook remains the broader coverage plan. Content below is a curated summary, not a verbatim page excerpt. No live search runs during these component evaluations.

source.title: Building effective agents — Anthropic
source.content: Curated summary, not a verbatim excerpt: Anthropic distinguishes workflows, in which code defines the paths through model and tool calls, from agents, in which a model dynamically directs its process and tool use. It recommends starting with simple patterns and adding complexity when it measurably improves results. Common workflow patterns include routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, and evaluator-optimizer. An evaluator-optimizer loop generates a candidate, evaluates it against clear criteria, and uses feedback to improve it. Loops are most useful when quality criteria are explicit and feedback can improve the result; they add latency and cost.

source.title: LangGraph interrupts
source.content: Curated summary, not a verbatim excerpt: LangGraph interrupt pauses execution and exposes a serializable payload to the caller. Durable human review requires a checkpointer and a thread_id. The application resumes the same thread using Command(resume=...), and the response becomes the interrupt return value. The node restarts from its beginning on resume, so work before interrupt can run again. Side effects before an interrupt should be idempotent or placed in a separate node. Human responses can approve a tool action or provide revised data, but the application must implement its own validation and business rules.

source.title: LangGraph persistence
source.content: Curated summary, not a verbatim excerpt: A LangGraph checkpointer saves graph state as checkpoints associated with a thread. A thread_id selects the persisted execution history. Persisted state enables human interaction, inspecting prior state, and fault recovery. These capabilities do not make arbitrary external side effects transactional or exactly once. A checkpointer should remain available across process restarts if the application must resume later. Checkpoint storage and an application's business records serve different purposes and can be stored separately.

source.title: OpenTelemetry traces
source.content: Curated summary, not a verbatim excerpt: A trace records the path of a request across operations. Spans represent operations and have start and end timestamps, identifiers, attributes, events, and status. Parent-child relationships connect spans within a trace. A failed tool call can be represented by an error status or event, helping an engineer locate a failure and inspect duration. A successful span says that the operation completed as instrumented; it does not by itself prove that an AI agent achieved the user's intended business outcome. Trace instrumentation can record sensitive inputs, so applications should choose what they store and redact secrets.

source.title: LangSmith evaluation concepts
source.content: Curated summary, not a verbatim excerpt: An evaluation dataset contains example inputs and can contain reference outputs and metadata. Reference outputs are used by evaluators rather than supplied as inputs to the application being tested. Evaluators can use code, a model, or human judgment to assess outputs. Offline evaluation runs an application against a dataset and compares experiments. Curating representative examples and reviewing evaluator behavior are part of building a useful evaluation process. A model score is a judgment under a rubric, not an objective guarantee of factual truth.

source.title: How to evaluate AI agents — NVIDIA
source.content: Curated summary, not a verbatim excerpt: Agent evaluation should assess whether the system completed the intended task across a sequence of actions. Final text and individual tool calls give only part of the picture. Checking the resulting environment or application state can establish whether a task was completed, such as whether the intended record or change exists. Tool correctness and process metrics help diagnose failures, while task completion addresses the outcome. Evaluation design depends on the task and available verification signals; there is no single text-only score that proves every agent succeeded.
